title: Lie dimension equals local dimension at a smooth identity
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $G$ a smooth $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $e\in G$ be the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ under its identity section. For the Lie algebra $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ [def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation], $\dim_k\operatorname{Lie}(G)=\dim\mathcal O_{G,e}$. Dimensions are interpreted in $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$, with the left side the cast of its finite vector-space dimension.

source.place: Dimension paragraph; sk-i-cartier third proof paragraph

proof.text: The identity section makes e rational. On an affine neighbourhood, identify the fibre of the relative cotangent sheaf with m/m² at e by the conormal sequence and its splitting over k. Its dual computes Lie(G); use rational tangent-cotangent duality to identify the two descriptions.

The smooth affine algebra has regular local ring at e. Its cotangent space is finite dimensional. Duality preserves finite dimension, and regularity equates cotangent dimension to local Krull dimension.
